commit.message:
M4 R1 recheck: deep-freeze the context's graphDiagnostics

The independent re-review of f8ada42 found graphDiagnostics frozen only shallowly: a holder of a
TrustedScoringContext could rewrite a diagnostic's message/code/entityIds and change a later report
under an unchanged inputFingerprint (an invalid code made scoreProject throw).

Fix: deepFreeze the diagnostics (and declaredTrackKeys, for uniformity). Audit of the other exposed
values: strings are immutable, rubric was already deep-frozen, reports are schema-parsed copies.
Six regression tests (group G in context.immutability.test.ts) cover frozen array/objects/entityIds,
message/code/path/entityIds mutation, array mutators, identical report + hashes afterwards, no
invalid code injectable, a recursive "nothing unfrozen" walk of every context property, and a report
that shares nothing with the context. Removing the fix makes 3 of them fail.

No formula, constant, version or architecture change.

commit.message:
M4 review round 1: immutable context snapshot, exact arithmetic, scale and locked-context validation

F1 (P1): the trusted scoring context no longer keeps caller-owned graph/known Maps. The factory
schema-parses and deep-freezes copies of the locked snapshot, the graph and the source facts BEFORE
integrity validation and fingerprinting, keeps the authoritative state in a module-private WeakMap,
and exposes no graph/known property.
F2 (P2): all arithmetic is exact rational (BigInt); thresholds are exact; reported numbers are rounded
once, exactly half-up. shareEpsilon removed.
F3 (P2): unsafe official scales (overflow, huge, subnormal spacing) are rejected with RUBRIC_INVALID.
F4 (P2): the locked snapshot must be schema-valid, status=locked, event/hash/version consistent
(LOCKED_CONTEXT_INVALID / LOCKED_CONTEXT_MISMATCH); SECURITY.md separates structural validation from
authenticity.
F6: the conservative overlap behavior is documented and pinned by a test.

Goldens regenerated (parametersHash changed; two exact ties now round up). No migration, no new
persistence, no model call, scoring-engine/v1 formulas and constants unchanged.

commit.message:
Implement scoring-engine/v1 as a pure Layer-2 package

dimension -> criterion -> overall aggregation with the approved policies:
official rubric wins whole and is never repaired or mixed with the fallback;
an official criterion is one atomic unit; an unweighted official rubric has no
official overall (explicit, labeled, unofficial equal-weight preview only on
request); insufficient evidence is a state, never a zero; not_applicable only
for the fallback Track criterion.

Evidence strength is V(effective level) x L(directness) x L(specificity); a
dimension's strength is the maximum over provenance groups, each as strong as
its most conservative member, so repetition never adds strength. Trust is
re-derived from structure: privileged labels resolve to unverified, claim
labels are never read, trusted attestations are internal and empty. Coverage
is measured only against declared needs; official criteria carry a labeled
citation-presence flag. Contradictions lower confidence, never the score.

The trusted context (rubric, graph, declared tracks) is built by a validating
factory, branded and frozen; the engine refuses anything else. Reports are
canonical JSON with parameters, rubric, input and graph hashes.

Tests: exhaustive ladder, published-weight invariants (the total, not each
weight), provenance grouping, trust, fail-closed validation, worked examples,
14 golden reports, cross-process determinism, seeded metamorphic properties
and model-trust-boundary guards.

commit.message:
Add scoring schemas: vocabularies, strict assessor input, report unions

Shared vocabularies as *_VALUES tuples plus Zod enums (directness, specificity,
evidence channel, rubric source, weight basis, states, insufficient reasons,
confidence basis, issue and diagnostic codes).

The only untrusted input is AssessorJudgmentsInput, a strict object with no
field for attestations, verification levels, weights, rubric content or track
declarations; unknown keys are an error. The report is a set of discriminated
unions in which an insufficient dimension, criterion or overall has no score
field at all, and the unofficial preview and the fixed notices are literals.

commit.message:
Revise M4 design to the approved decisions; clarify SCORING.md policy

M4 design revision 2 (no formula code):
- D1 unweighted official rubric: no official overall; explicit unofficial
  equal-weight preview only on request, reported outside `overall`.
- D2 Option A: trusted attestations are internal and empty, not a caller or
  model input; unattested privileged labels never raise effective trust.
- D3/D4/D11: official criteria are atomic units; no official/fallback mixing;
  `not_applicable` Track only for the versioned fallback rubric.
- D5: no invented evidence needs for official criteria; a labeled
  citation-presence proxy replaces coverage there.
- D6/D7: 36 fallback dimensions kept as provisional versioned heuristics with
  stated limitations (needs unsatisfiable before M7); parameters are heuristics.
- D8: item-level noisy-OR replaced by the maximum effective strength of
  distinct cited evidence (ten team statements: 0.9865 -> 0.35).
- D9/D10: linear official-scale assumption documented; a scored judgment with
  no usable citation becomes insufficient_evidence, judged value diagnostic only.
- Added guards: unmapped contradictions stay visible, no completeness claim,
  fail-closed citations; corrected metamorphic properties; all worked examples
  recomputed.

docs/SCORING.md: policy wording only (status banner, precedence item 6, the
official-rubric adaptation note in section 4, new section 12). No formulas.

commit.message:
Add M4 prerequisite A (consistent graph reads) and M4 design proposal

Prerequisite A: EvidenceGraphStore.loadGraph now reads the project, the five
graph tables and every provenance lookup inside ONE read-only REPEATABLE READ
transaction, so a batch committed mid-read can no longer be half visible (false
DANGLING_REFERENCE, silently missing contradictions). createGraph is unchanged
and stays READ COMMITTED: its FOR NO KEY UPDATE lock depends on it.

Tests: transaction shape, createGraph isolation guard, deterministic
interleaving with a committing writer for each graph table, stress test with
concurrent writers and readers, failure cleanup, connection-leak check, and a
read-only check (PostgreSQL 16 and PGlite). Mutation proofs: dropping the
transaction fails 11 tests; moving createGraph to REPEATABLE READ fails the
isolation guard and the cap race.

Prerequisite B (audit only, no schema change): characterization tests for what
direct SQL can store (privileged levels without evidence, a self-consistent
machine_verified chain that passes validateGraphIntegrity, README-anchored
repo_corroborated, supersession laundering of a contradiction).

docs/milestones/M4-design.md proposes scoring-engine/v1 policies, formulas,
worked examples, file plan and the decisions that need owner approval. No
scoring code is implemented.

commit.message:
Harden M3 evidence integrity

Fixes the three P1 blockers from the independent hostile review. The original
M3 commit is kept intact.

P1-1  machine_verified trust boundary. A span proves provenance, not that the
      evidence text or a claim is true, so a producer must not grant a
      trusted-observation level by choosing the enum value. The planner (and so
      EvidenceGraphStore.createGraph) now refuses machine_verified,
      judge_verified and live_verified on evidence and claims
      (VERIFICATION_NOT_AVAILABLE); the vocabulary, rule tables and transition
      matrix are unchanged for the future trusted path. repo_corroborated now
      needs a repository source-code artifact: a conservative, fail-closed
      classification from the real M2 key/kind/media type treats README, docs,
      markdown/rst/txt/adoc and metadata artifacts as non-corroborating.
      Synthetic Atlas demo reframed to repo_corroborated / unverified.

P1-2  Per-project writers. createGraph locked the project with FOR SHARE, which
      does not serialize writers (12 racers at 1999/2000 wrote 2011 claims).
      It now takes FOR NO KEY UPDATE as its first locking operation. Real
      PostgreSQL connection tests cover the cap race, lock compatibility,

commit.message:
Finish M2 security hardening

Final pre-merge fixes from the M2 security audit.

A1  StructuredText trimmed with /\s+$/, which backtracks quadratically on a
    long whitespace run that is not at the end (16-20 s at 1 MiB). Use the
    linear trimEnd(); regression tests cover the extraction paths and the
    capture worker.
B2  The pinned transport now sets rejectUnauthorized: true for HTTPS, so
    NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 cannot disable certificate checks. A real
    self-signed TLS server must still be refused and never receives the
    Authorization header.
B5  The GitHub adapter ingests public repositories only: anything not clearly
    public is rejected (unsupported_source / private_repository) right after
    the repository metadata, with no artifacts and no further request.
B8  CaptureQueue.finalize never writes terminal timestamps earlier than the
    stored created_at / started_at (1 ms floor for PostgreSQL microseconds),
    in every branch, including emergency finalization and the lease reaper.
B13 AUTH_MODE=dev requires a loopback API_HOST regardless of NODE_ENV.
B1  An IPv6 address must lie in 2000::/3 in addition to the existing
    ipaddr.js range and denylist checks.

Remaining P2 findings are listed in docs/milestones/M2-report.md.

commit.message:
Harden M2 capture safety

Fixes the merge blockers from the M2 hostile review.

P0-1 HTML/Devpost parsing is structurally bounded: one iterative traversal
(each node visited once, no whole-tree selectors, capped collectors, a
400,000-node budget) replaces quadratic querySelectorAll use; over budget it
degrades deterministically and the snapshot is partial with the new reason
html_structure_limit (migration 0006). A 1 MiB hostile page went from
22-70 s to under half a second.

P1-1 tree.json is listed within a 3 MiB byte budget (partial /
tree_entry_limit instead of failed / internal_error); entries inside ignored
directories no longer spend the entry cap or the budget.

P1-2 database-invalid text (U+0000, unpaired surrogates) is replaced by U+FFFD
and recorded in metadata.contentSanitization instead of failing the snapshot;
finalization errors are never logged raw (ids and SQLSTATE only) and a failed
finalization is recorded as a sanitized failure in a second transaction.

P1-3 the web UI scripts bind 127.0.0.1 explicitly; a regression test and the
docs state that exposing it is unsupported until real user authentication.

P1-4 a direct API/PostgreSQL regression test pins the artifact ordering
(COLLATE "C"), with a canary that the database collation differs.

Open P2 findings are listed in docs/milestones/M2-report.md.

commit.message:
Order snapshot artifacts by byte order regardless of database locale

The snapshot detail endpoint (and the worker fixture test helper) sorted
artifact keys with the database's default collation. On a PostgreSQL
cluster initialized with en_US.utf8 (as in CI) "files/README.md" sorted
after lowercase paths, so artifact listings depended on server locale.
Sort with COLLATE "C" so the order is deterministic everywhere.

commit.message:
Harden Event Context rebuild safety

Addresses the PR #1 review findings for the M1 Event Context build.

Rebuilds no longer silently erase human review. A build compares the
reviewed draft with its last extraction baseline using canonical JSON
(a document without a baseline, e.g. hand-authored or copied from a
locked version, counts as reviewed). Replacing reviewed changes is
refused with 409 HUMAN_EDITS_WOULD_BE_REPLACED unless the request sets
replaceHumanEdits: true (default false). An explicit replacement is
recorded in the event_context_built audit metadata. No automatic merge.

Builds are optimistically guarded. The source-set and draft-state
fingerprints are taken before the extractor runs (with no transaction
open) and re-checked under FOR UPDATE before writing. If the sources or
the draft changed meanwhile (a source added, a human edit, another
build), the result is discarded with 409 CONTEXT_BUILD_STALE, the run is
cancelled and event_context_build_cancelled records the reason. A
version locked mid-build is cancelled the same way.

The review UI warns when a rebuild would replace reviewed changes and
requires an explicit checkbox plus "Rebuild and replace my reviewed
draft". Docs and the M1 report are updated; regression tests cover
refusal, confirmed replacement, stale edits, stale sources, overlapping
builds and locking mid-build on PGlite and PostgreSQL 16.

commit.message:
Initialize Judge Copilot architecture foundation

Milestone 0: engineering foundation and architecture encoding. No judging
functionality, model calls, integrations, scoring or authentication.

- pnpm workspace with strict TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier and Vitest
- apps/api: Fastify with GET /health and graceful shutdown
- apps/worker: idle worker that boots and stops cleanly
- apps/web: Next.js placeholder page
- packages/schemas: Score10, Ratio and the foundational domain vocabularies
- packages/domain: inferred domain types and lifecycle classifications
- packages/shared: env validation, redacting structured logger, shutdown
- packages/audit: append-only audit event contract and AuditSink port
- packages/database: Drizzle schema and migrations for events,
  event_context_versions, analysis_runs and audit_events (append-only)
- tests: schema, migration (PGlite, optional real Postgres), API, worker,
  process-boot, dependency-direction and no-network guard tests
- docs: PRODUCT, ARCHITECTURE, SCORING, AI_PIPELINE, SECURITY, V1_CONTRACT,
  M0 milestone report, and agent guardrails (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)
